sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Medical Device FDA 510(k) Filing and European CE Mark Compliance

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BELUUM-Luxembourg Economic Union bilateral investment treaties, including the BLEU-China BIT (entered into force in 2009)
Luxembourg double taxation conventions in force with more than 80 jurisdictions, including the United States, Germany, France, China and the Netherlands
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (provisionally applied since September 2017)
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force since February 1, 2019)
EU-South Korea Free Trade Agreement (in force since December 13, 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 concerning the Register of Commerce and Companies and the accounting and reporting obligations of undertakings, as amended; Grand-Ducal implementing regulations concerning the filing, access and updating of the Register of Beneficial Owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or extract from the commercial register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority in the originating country, or full consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of compliance of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry, tax authority or corporate registrar in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, preceded by notarization of the certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or equivalent register extract identifying the officers, directors and signatories of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, registered agent or companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, preceded by notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and articles of association / statutes of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered office or corporate secretary of the shareholder, confirmed by a notary public in the originating jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, preceded by notarial certification of consistency

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg notary and incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder's board of directors or general meeting, notarized in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport or national identity document of every ultimate beneficial owner, director and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national civil registry / passport authority of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a notary public in the origin country, followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization where requested by the Luxembourg notary or banks

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD under the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law requires identification and verification of all beneficial owners, officers and commercial counterparties of the proposed SARL, with screening against the European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List and the Luxembourg national list of persons subject to asset freezes. Politically exposed persons, including domestic and foreign PEPs, must be identified and, where relevant, subject to enhanced due diligence applicable to the proposed MedTech regulatory consultancy. Given the low-risk profile of ISIC 7490 advisory activities, standard AML documentation is normally sufficient, but source-of-funds and source-of-wealth checks may be required if the owner is a legal vehicle, a trust or a non-resident intermediary.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) via www.lbr.lu and the eJustice.lu company registration module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Luxembourg company names must be written using the Latin alphabet and must be unequivocally distinguishable from names already recorded in the RCSL. The official administrative languages are French, German and Luxembourgish; non-Latin script names, when used as commercial names, must be transliterated into Latin characters for RCSL indexing. Every SARL must include in its corporate name either the full statutory term 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the LBR/RCSL rejects or objects to a proposed name, the applicant, through the designated Luxembourg notary, may first submit an alternative name reservation through the online portal. A formal written refusal may be challenged under Luxembourg administrative procedure by filing a written request for reconsideration with the Luxembourg Business Registers within fifteen days from notification. Where the administrative refusal is maintained, an appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within three months of notification, and thereafter to the administrative court of appeal, in accordance with the Law of 1 December 2015 on administrative procedure and the Law of 19 December 2002 concerning the Register of Commerce and Companies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted only if combined with a licensed domiciliation agent and a genuine Luxembourg administrative centre; it may satisfy RCSL registered-office requirements but does not by itself provide sufficient economic substance. For a non-regulated FDA/CE regulatory consultancy, a virtual office is pragmatically admissible for initial registration, but banks, auditors and tax authorities require decision-making, board activity, accounting records and operational management to be traceable in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate, estimated at approximately 12% annual likelihood for a non-regulated low-risk consultancy with no local employees. Unannounced physical inspections are more probable where the UBO is not Luxembourg-resident, where no independent local management exists, or where filing inconsistencies appear in the RBE register or VAT filings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL name search and negative certificate / non-opposition certificate for the proposed corporate name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff for name verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting of the articles of association, notarization of the incorporation deed and attendance at deed signing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff based on company capital and professional scale, market benchmark EUR 1,500 to EUR 2,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL electronic incorporation filing and publication in the Luxembourg Official electronic register
Initial beneficial owner register declaration with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening, and verification of beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / approved AML professional
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, hourly EUR 250 to EUR 450

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign corporate documents into French, German or Luxembourgish as required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent certified translator and/or Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per translated page and certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority or consulate in the originating jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official state fee per document, estimated per shareholder bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office / domiciliation service commitment fee for the first quarter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Service contract based on prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016 and the Law of 23 September 2020; SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 to 710-25; electronic incorporation governed by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte notarié de constitution) filed by the notary with the RCS via the LBR electronic portal and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SARL minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up; cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution or with the notary (compte séquestre) until registration, evidenced by a certificate of deposit. Reduced minimum capital of EUR 1 is available for a micro-SARL under the 2016 reform where all shareholders are natural persons and the applicable small-entity thresholds are met.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the statutory incorporation of [•] SARL be and is hereby ratified, including the draft articles of association, valuation of contributions, and the full subscription of the share capital of EUR 12,000, deposited in a blocked account with a Luxembourg credit institution. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the corporate purpose (medical device regulatory consulting, including FDA 510(k) and CE Mark compliance services) be adopted. RESOLVED, that [name] be and is hereby appointed Gérant (Manager) for an indefinite term, with full power to act singly, to sign the notarial deed, file the registration with the RCS, apply for VAT, social security, and any establishment permits, and to execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Legalization of the Incorporation File
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) in coordination with corporate counsel; LBR e-incorporation portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct Luxembourg counsel to draft the articles of association, corporate purpose, and capital structure for an SARL under the Law of 10 August 1915. Submit the draft to the notary for pre-approval and mandatory anti-money-laundering verification of the ultimate beneficial owners. The notary schedules the execution date and issues the file checklist. All foreign-language documents must be translated into French or German; foreign public documents require legalization or apostille.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Valid passport or national ID of all shareholders and the proposed Gérant
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
AML/KYC forms and ultimate beneficial owner declaration
Business plan evidencing the corporate purpose under ISIC 7490 (MedTech regulatory consulting)
Power of attorney for non-resident shareholders, legalized or apostilled
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the bar association queries the file, counsel shall revise the articles or UBO documentation and resubmit within 15 calendar days; any deficiency letter is cured by a supplementary declaration or amended draft.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Bank Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank of the Company's choice) or the notary's escrow account (compte séquestre).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation ('[•] SARL en formation') with a Luxembourg bank. Transfer the EUR 12,000 minimum capital by auditable wire transfer from the shareholders' accounts. Obtain the bank's certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage). The funds remain blocked until the RCS issues the registration extract; the bank releases the funds upon production of the RCS certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of company name reservation issued by the RCS
AML/KYC documents of all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Proof of source of funds (payslips, sale agreements, or bank statements)
Completed bank account opening forms and blocked deposit instruction letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide additional source-of-wealth documentation; if the name reservation expires during bank review, re-file the name reservation with the RCS and restart the holding period only if the reserved name has been released.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) — compulsory for SARL formation under the Law of 10 August 1915.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary authenticates the deed of incorporation, verifies the identity of all parties and the legality of the corporate purpose, confirms receipt of the certificate of deposit, and collects physical or proxy signatures. The deed is executed in French (customary) and must state the subscribed capital, the articles, the registered office, the Gérant appointment, and the prohibited articles if a micro-SARL is formed. Immediately after execution, the notary proceeds with the electronic filing to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of deposit of share capital (attestation de blocage)
AML/UBO declarations executed by each shareholder
Notarized or apostilled power of attorney for proxy signatories
Final draft deed approved by counsel
Evidence of payment of notary fees, registration fees, and state fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries or rejects the deed, the notary prepares a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) or a supplemental declaration within 5 business days, and the corrected deed is re-filed without loss of priority if filed within the RCS deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the RCS and Publication in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the RCS; publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the authenticated deed to the LBR electronic platform together with the required forms (list of Gérants, capital certificate, registered office consent). The RCS examines the filing, assigns the registration number and extracts, and publishes the deed in the RESA. Legal personality is acquired as of the RCS registration; the publication completes the third-party notice requirement.
required_dossiers: Authenticated notarial deed of incorporation (submitted by the notary)
Certificate of deposit of share capital (annexed to the deed)
Certified list of Gérants with biographical data (form)
Landlord's consent to the registered office address
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query for data mismatch or missing annexes, the notary corrects and re-submits within 5 business days; if registration is refused, the company may apply to the competent district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) for judicial review within 40 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Operational Registrations (VAT, Establishment Permit, Social Security, LuxTrust)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des classes moyennes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); LuxTrust S.A.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS extract is obtained: (i) file Form 606 with the AEDT to obtain the VAT number for B2B consulting services; (ii) apply for the general business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement, category 'commerçant') under the Law of 2 September 2011; (iii) register the Gérant and any employees with the CCSS; (iv) subscribe to a LuxTrust certificate for eGovernment and eDelivery; (v) if processing health-related personal data for clients, declare the processing to the National Commission for Data Protection (CNPD).
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (extrait)
Certified copy of the articles of association
Identification of the Gérant and certificate of good conduct (no criminal record)
Registered office lease agreement
VAT form 606 and establishment permit application form
LuxTrust identity verification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit application is suspended or refused, the company may file a supplementary economic and professional qualifications file with the Ministry of the Economy and, if still unsuccessful, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within 3 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to the described office-based regulatory consulting scope (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541690). The general competent authority for any commercial activity in Luxembourg is the Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des classes moyennes (general business establishment permit); the industrial licensing board (Administration de l'environnement) governs only installations classées.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General business establishment permit (Autorisation d'établissement) - category 'Commerçant' under the Law of 2 September 2011; no separate industrial operating permit or agrément industriel is triggered by intellectual MedTech regulatory consulting services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), operating under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity comprises solely office-based professional consultancy with no manufacturing, no installations classées, and no point-source emissions; a full or simplified EIA is not triggered under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at the registered office stage. If an ancillary laboratory, demo facility, or any installation classée is later established, compliance thresholds under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 November 1994 on wastewater discharge, EU REACH/CLP for chemical substances, and the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Class B low-occupancy office clearance: the landlord must provide the building fire safety dossier (dossier de sécurité) confirming compliance with the Law of 4 July 2017 on building safety. If the entity subsequently occupies a building with public access or high occupancy, a fire safety approval from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS) is mandatory. Workplace clearance under the Labour Code is evidenced by the employer's registration with the CCSS for occupational accident coverage and the mandatory workplace health and safety declaration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (IMT) and net wealth tax (IS); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises for customs and export formalities; unified electronic access via MyGuichet.lu, the Luxembourg Business Registers portal at www.lbr.lu, and the ACD/AEDT online services at impotsdirects.public.lu and pbl.public.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Notarially incorporate the SARL and register with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) to obtain the Luxembourg business registration number (matricule RCS). 2) File the VAT registration application (form 100 or the MyGuichet electronic declaration) with the AEDT to obtain the national VAT identification number (format LU followed by 8 digits); a non-EU-established corporate parent or foreign branch may be required to appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative or to establish a fixed establishment for VAT purposes. 3) Register as an employer with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for social-security contributions and with the ACD for salary-withholding tax; the SARL is simultaneously registered ex officio with the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax upon notification of its registered office and corporate objects. 4) Activate the electronic filing channels (MyGuichet, eCDF, eTVA) and reconcile the RCS matricule with the VAT number and the CCSS employer registration for the monthly withholding and VAT declaration cycle.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or pass-through election exists: a Luxembourg SARL is irrebuttably treated as an entity-level corporate taxpayer subject to IRC, IMT, solidarity surcharge and net wealth tax on its worldwide income, with the participation exemption available for qualifying EU and third-country dividends and capital gains. Available statutory elections relevant to a MedTech regulatory consulting SARL include: (i) waiver of the EUR 35,000 VAT small-business exemption in favour of normal VAT registration; (ii) formation of a VAT group (assujetti unique) under the Luxembourg VAT law where financial, economic and organisational links exist; (iii) alignment and elective relief elections under the Luxembourg hybrid-mismatch rules (Articles 168ter to 168septies of the LIR, implementing ATAD 1 and ATAD 2); and (iv) the participation-exemption election exercised through the annual corporate income tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 VAT-exclusive annual taxable turnover within Luxembourg for the small-business exemption; mandatory VAT registration applies once this threshold is exceeded; non-established foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg have no registration threshold; the EU cross-border B2C distance-sales threshold of EUR 10,000 also applies; B2B supplies rendered to customers established outside the EU are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT and therefore do not count toward the registration threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance engine, digital stamping or API-based e-invoice validation is currently in force for domestic Luxembourg B2B supplies; mandatory B2G electronic invoicing has applied to invoices addressed to Luxembourg public entities since 1 January 2023 (structured Peppol BIS 3.0 or equivalent format); since 2024 taxable persons must be able to receive structured electronic invoices; Luxembourg is transposing the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework, which will introduce transaction-based digital reporting and mandatory e-invoicing for domestic supplies as of 2030 and for cross-border supplies as of 2035.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (a) physical exports of goods definitively dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU customs territory under Article 63 of the Luxembourg VAT law (transposing Article 146 of the VAT Directive), provided the exporter holds evidence that the goods left the EU within 90 days of dispatch; and (b) B2B services, including FDA 510(k) filing and CE Mark regulatory consulting, supplied to a customer established outside the EU, because the place of supply follows the customer's place of establishment under Article 44 of the VAT Directive and the supply is therefore outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (economically 0%). Eligibility requires written proof of the customer's non-EU establishment (valid local VAT or tax registration certificate, certificate of residence, or equivalent official document), a signed consulting contract defining the regulatory filing scope, and itemised documentation evidencing services actually rendered. Services supplied to EU-established customers do not qualify and remain taxable by reverse charge in the customer's member state under Article 196 of the VAT Directive.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) electronically lodged in the AES/ICS export system with the Administration des douanes et accises naming the exporting SARL as consignor
Transport and exit evidence: Bill of Lading (sea freight), Air Waybill (airfreight), CMR consignment note (road), or written confirmation from the customs office of exit
Commercial invoice with Incoterms, packing list and, where applicable, a Certificate of Free Sale or export licence for medical devices
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT credit advice, or foreign-currency inward remittance proof evidencing settlement of the export receivable

For zero-rated offshore consulting services: signed services contract, itemised debit note, customer VAT or tax registration certificate or non-EU residence certificate, and the regulatory file reference such as the FDA 510(k) submission number or CE/Notified Body certificate reference
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT law does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline, but a 180-day inward-remittance settlement window is the documentary benchmark applied by the AEDT and Luxembourg banks when accepting zero-rating evidence; failure to show payment settlement within this window materially weakens the substantiation file and exposes the invoices to retrospective VAT reassessment. Export zero-rating and offshore-service invoicing are high-priority audit targets: the AEDT may claw back the VAT with statutory late interest for up to the general 6-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in fraud cases, and may impose administrative penalties of 25% to 100% of the evaded VAT under Articles 398 to 400 of the General Tax Law. Fraudulent intent exposes the SARL and its managers to criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years; customs offences additionally attract fines of up to double the customs debt or the value of the goods under the Union Customs Code and Luxembourg customs legislation; participation in round-tripping or carrousel-type export chains may result in joint and several liability and denial of zero-rating for the entire invoice chain.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank, operating within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism of the European Central Bank (ECB). Foreign exchange and payment oversight is jointly exercised by the BCL and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which supervises credit institutions, payment institutions, and electronic money institutions in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) enjoys unrestricted convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions in Luxembourg. There are no exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements, and no surrender obligations under national law. Full liberalisation of capital movements and payments is guaranteed by Articles 63 to 65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), subject only to the exceptional safeguard measures of Articles 64(2) and 66 TFEU, none of which are currently in force. Profit remittance by a SARL is not subject to exchange-control approval; the only hurdles are standard corporate formalities, namely (i) the statutory net-asset solvency test, (ii) the general meeting's distribution resolution, (iii) possible Luxembourg dividend withholding tax of 15% (reducible under an applicable double tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where conditions are met), and (iv) the bank's AML/KYC source-of-funds verification. Cross-border payments to or from sanctioned persons or entities are blocked under EU restrictive measures as enforced by the CSSF; therefore, counterparty sanctions screening is an implicit prerequisite to convertibility in practice.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate or surrender export proceeds or service-fee receipts. The SARL may lawfully maintain EUR and USD balances in Luxembourg and abroad without BCL approval. The only compliance burden is statistical: credit institutions report balance-of-payments data to the BCL for individual client transactions exceeding the €12,500 direct-reporting threshold, and the SARL should accurately state payment purpose codes for these filings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (with segregated capital-deposit sub-ledger for the €12,000 minimum statutory capital)
Operational Account + Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué for incorporation capital)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. A Luxembourg-authorised electronic money institution (EMI) or an EU-passported payment service provider (PSP) such as Airwallex, Payoneer, or PayPal Business can serve the SARL's low-risk consulting fee collections (bank wire and credit card rails) and provide multi-currency receiving accounts in EUR and USD. However, the EMI route has material legal constraints: (i) under Directive 2009/110/EC Article 6(3), an EMI may grant credit only when incidental and strictly limited to €150 per transaction and €500 aggregate outstanding at any time, so no overdraft or working capital facility is available; (ii) EMIs cannot provide FX hedging or term-deposit treasury products, which must be arranged with a credit institution; (iii) USD clearing is dependent on unregulated correspondent chains and may trigger enhanced OFAC screening; (iv) the EMI's onboarding relies on the same CSSF AML/CTF framework (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended), so UBO and source-of-fund checks are not waived; and (v) the BCL balance-of-payments reporting obligation rests ultimately on the SARL's accounting records, requiring the SARL to retain all payment purpose and counterparty data itself. Consequently, the EMI is viable as a collection-side overlay rail but is not a substitute for a full tier-1 corporate banking relationship in Luxembourg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically before the bank in Luxembourg; the Law of 25 March 2020 on digitalisation permits remote client onboarding using eIDAS-compliant electronic identity means and video-verification procedures. In practice, however, Luxembourg banks exercise discretionary risk appetite: Spuerkeess and BIL generally accept remote onboarding for a low-risk professional-services SARL with non-resident shareholders, provided at least one manager or authorised signatory completes a live video KYC interview, the passports and proof-of-address documents are notarised or apostilled, and the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extracts are produced. BGL BNP Paribas and Société Générale Luxembourg typically require at least one physical meeting at their Luxembourg premises for a newly incorporated entity whose ultimate beneficial owners are non-EEA residents. For US-resident shareholders, an apostilled and certified corporate file, a notarised power of attorney for the Luxembourg resident manager, and a physical visit by the manager are normally demanded. Anticipated onboarding timeline: four to eight weeks from complete document submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership and source of capital injection for a non-resident shareholder funding the €12,000 minimum statutory capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of incorporation, RBE extract confirming the ultimate beneficial owners, audited recent bank statements of the contributing shareholder, a sworn source-of-wealth statement covering net worth and professional occupation, certified passports of all beneficial owners, apostilled corporate registration documents, and a CSSF-compliant declaration of no adverse media, sanctions, or PEP exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US counterparty exposure in the client base under FDA 510(k) submission work, triggering enhanced US sanctions and anti-money-laundering scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg RBE extract, a written AML/CFT business risk assessment classifying the activity as ISIC 7490 low-risk regulatory consulting, executed engagement letters with each medical device manufacturer client, a flow-of-funds memorandum showing FDA user fees as pass-through disbursements, OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening results for every US counterparty, and copies of the SARL's professional indemnity insurance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the declared consulting purpose and expected high-value cross-border wire activity (USD FDA fees and EUR notified-body fees), which may resemble regulated financial intermediation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended articles of association (statuts) expressly limiting the corporate purpose to FDA 510(k) and CE Mark regulatory consulting, signed consultation agreements with detailed scope and fee schedules, issued invoices with precise service descriptions, a transfer-pricing file demonstrating arm's-length billing, a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming that no MiFID, payment-services, or e-money licence is required, and a copy of the VAT registration certificate confirming the service nature of the revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds between the SARL operating account and US FDA lockbox accounts, potentially flagged under transaction-monitoring rules as unusual layering activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy memorandum describing the FDA fee payment calendar and the EUR/USD hedging policy, a consolidated schedule of regulatory filings and associated government fees, the original FDA 510(k) submission receipts and Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) payment confirmations, and a written undertaking to maintain a complete audit trail for all cross-border transactions above the BCL's €12,500 reporting threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (i) the shareholder's originating bank sends an SWIFT MT103 wire in EUR to the SARL's EUR IBAN at a Luxembourg tier-1 bank; (ii) the payment must carry a transparent purpose code such as 'Capital injection / CJ01' or the BCL balance-of-payments code for equity capital contributions, and the beneficiary account must be identified as the blocked capital escrow sub-account pending RCS registration; (iii) the Luxembourg receiving bank will hold funds on deposit blocked in favour of the notary until the deed of incorporation is filed with the RCS and the minimum capital certificate is delivered; (iv) the bank will require the notarised share subscription deed, the notary's attestation of full payment, updated RBE filings made within one month of any UBO change, and the business plan before lifting the block; (v) all deposit and release events must be reported by the bank to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics if the transaction exceeds the €12,500 threshold. For subsequent consultant-fee inflows and client credits exceeding the threshold, the SARL should instruct clients to state purpose code 'Service fee / S010' with the contract reference so as to avoid AML misclassification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade and regulatory settlements: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant (up to €100,000 per transaction) for disbursements to EU beneficiaries, including notified bodies for CE Mark reviews and EU-based subcontractors; (ii) SWIFT MT103 via a USD correspondent bank (typically CHIPS or Fedwire in the United States) for submission of FDA user fees to the US Department of Health and Human Services through the US Treasury lockbox, using the Treasury concentration bank's ABA routing (e.g., Citibank New York, ABA 021000089); (iii) Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) where the SARL imports physical medical device prototypes or pre-finances testing equipment, with the LC issued against shipping and inspection documents; (iv) EURO1/STEP2 high-value clearing for urgent cross-border corporate payments in EUR above the SEPA Instant cap; and (v) credit-card acquiring rails (Visa and Mastercard through a Luxembourg or EU-passported PSP, PCI DSS compliant) for inbound consulting-fee collection, with settlement to the SARL's operational account in EUR or, where enabled by the PSP, in USD before an internal exchange into EUR.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Deliverable EUR/USD FX Forward — OTC instrument executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a bank's short-form FX Master Agreement with a CSSF-regulated credit institution; permitted without prior authorisation for a non-financial counterparty (NFC-), and exempt from the EMIR clearing obligation so long as the SARL's rolling average gross notional remains below the €3 billion per-asset-class clearing threshold, which is far above the SARL's anticipated fee volumes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (comptes annuels): approved balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés — RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance-sheet date (calendar-year SARL: by 31 July of the following year); shareholders' approval meeting must be held within 6 months (by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge invoiced by the RCS; criminal fines of approximately EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 under the Law of 19 December 2002; prosecutor's injunction to file; non-filing for two consecutive financial years permits judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO declaration annual confirmation and update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs), including post-transfer registry update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs — RBE), administered through Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration within 1 month of RCS registration; annual confirmation on the RBE calendar cycle; any share transfer or change of control reported within 1 month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance sanctions under the Law of 13 January 2019 and the AML/CFT framework: fines in the range of EUR 125 to EUR 125,000, publication of penalties, and personal liability of managers for false or late declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' general meeting approving the annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the SARL; minutes kept at the registered office (no separate RCS filing unless the meeting resolves capital-structure changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory meeting within 6 months of the financial-year end (calendar-year SARL: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting and approve the accounts renders the gérant(s) civilly liable for resulting damages and may constitute a serious management failure supporting judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory registers audit and maintenance: share register (registre des associés), minutes book, and management records verified and brought current
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office; registers remain inspectable by the RCS, tax authorities, and AML/CFT supervisory bodies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous maintenance with mandatory notation of each share transfer upon occurrence; full reconciliation and audit of registers at the annual meeting cycle (within 6 months of year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or missing statutory registers violate the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Commercial Code, exposing managers to court-ordered fines, adverse evidentiary consequences, and civil liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an independent approved auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) where the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50. Audit is also compulsory if requested by a qualifying shareholder, for consolidated group requirements, or under sectoral rules (e.g., financial services). Companies below the thresholds qualify as small undertakings and are exempt from the statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2008 on annual and consolidated accounts (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for statutory annual accounts and mandatory for certain consolidated groups and listed or regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Law of 13 January 2019 and its implementing regulations, every SARL must confirm the accuracy of its RBE beneficial-ownership declaration on the annual confirmation cycle and must file an updated declaration within one month of any change, including share transfers that alter the 25% ownership, voting, or control analysis. The gérant(s) are responsible for ensuring the RBE entry reflects the share register at all times.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associés) recording shareholdings, pledges, and transfers.
Register of Managers/Directors recording appointments, resignations, and powers of the gérant(s).
Minute Book containing shareholder meeting resolutions and management decisions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – USD 5,500 per annum for a professional Luxembourg domiciliation/service-agent arrangement including registered office, correspondence handling, and compliance-calendar management.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 for a certified statutory audit of a small-to-mid-size SARL; exempt small companies typically pay USD 1,500 – USD 4,000 for a voluntary review or accountant's attestation report.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate rate for Luxembourg City (domestic CIT 15% on first EUR 175,000 and 17% on excess, plus 7% solidarity surcharge and 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; IP Box yields 80% exemption on qualifying net IP income (effective ~5%); investment tax credit up to 8% for eligible tangible assets; participation exemption for qualifying dividend income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 750 (CIT and municipal business tax) plus Form 740 (net wealth tax) e-filed through MyGuichet (myguichet.lu) using LuxTrust digital certificate
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the administration requires filing by 31 May of the following year, extensions available upon request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, registered office, RCS number, Luxembourg VAT and tax file number, fiscal year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) must identify the PE, its address, and the head-office jurisdiction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residence status and accounting period: resident/domestic versus non-resident PE classification, start and end dates of the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents declare income attributable to the Luxembourg PE only; calendar-year PE accounts should mirror the head-office reporting period

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result before deductions: worldwide profit for residents, PE-allocable profit for non-residents, adjusted for commercial-law depreciation, provisions, and currency effects
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Luxembourg PE's business profit, excluding foreign-source portfolio income not subject to Luxembourg domestic tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, exemptions and loss carryforward: participation exemption, IP Box exemption, investment credit, and tax-loss offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may offset PE losses only against Luxembourg PE profits; no offset against foreign head-office income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income and tax: application of 15% on the first EUR 175,000 and 17% on the excess, then solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE must compute municipal business tax on the PE's taxable base; CIT surcharge applies prorated to the PE's allocable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing schedule and related-party transactions: disclosure of intercompany revenue/costs, counterparties, jurisdictions, and transfer-pricing methodology used
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a Luxembourg PE must report all intercompany agreements of the PE and confirm arm's length substance; attach the TP Local File when thresholds are triggered

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a default tax assessment with a surcharge of 10% to 20% of the assessed tax, late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, and a possible administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 for continued failure to cooperate with the tax authority

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% general domestic rate; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥10% holding, 12-month minimum) and under most DTTs with substantial corporate shareholdings; treaty rates for portfolio investors often between 5% and 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before distribution, the non-resident shareholder must deliver a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its country of residence to the Luxembourg paying agent. To invoke the EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption, the shareholder must submit to the Luxembourg tax administration an exemption application together with the TRC, a sworn confirmation of the qualified shareholding, and evidence of the 12-month holding period. Any tax withheld at the wrong rate may be reclaimed by filing a refund request within the statutory limitation period (generally five years)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not levy domestic withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments (0%). Payments to non-cooperative EU-listed jurisdictions may be subject to a defensive 20% withholding, subject to any applicable treaty override and anti-abuse rules

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File must be prepared and maintained where the annual book value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds EUR 500,000; Master File obligations apply to groups with consolidated turnover of EUR 750 million or more
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies economic substance analysis rather than annual ESR filings: the availability of IP Box benefits, the 0% Parent-Subsidiary exemption, treaty access, and participation exemption depends on genuine premises, operative staff, actual business-risk control, and decision-making in Luxembourg (Art. 56 LIR; ATAD and MLI/PPT)

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Luxembourg-source revenue, fabricating deductions, or creating artificial losses to eliminate corporate income tax liability in the SARL
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment plus a penalty of 50% to 100% of the evaded tax; criminal fine from EUR 10,000 to EUR 100,000; imprisonment up to five years under Article 1093 LIR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false or incomplete returns are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax and penalties; courts may impose travel bans, disqualification from board positions, and custodial sentences in aggravated cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL exclusively as an invoice platform for foreign related parties, with no local staff, no operational premises, and no exercise of managerial control over the FDA/CE regulatory consulting services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the entity for Luxembourg tax purposes; recharacterization of payments as deemed dividends subject to 15% WHT; retroactive interest and punitive penalties up to EUR 100,000 under abuse-of-law rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the resulting barriers to withholding tax if they directed funds abroad while retaining no economic substance; personal asset confiscation can follow a fraud conviction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting management fees, royalties, or service margins to a foreign affiliate without an arm's length comparability analysis, or failing to maintain required TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax primary adjustment, secondary adjustment, exclusion of deduction, late interest, and a negligence penalty of 20% to 50% of the underpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sanctioned the misstatement can be assessed jointly for the penalty share and prosecuted for tax fraud; a civil clawback extends to personal assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using bank wire or credit card payment rails to launder corrupt foreign payments, circumvent EU sanctions, or conceal the ultimate beneficiary of consultancy fees, without proper customer due diligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Entity-level administrative fine up to EUR 1 million or 10% of annual turnover; freezing of assets and disgorgement; referral to the Public Prosecutor for criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face up to five years' imprisonment for money laundering, personal monetary liability for both the entity's obligations and state claims, and an EU-wide prohibition on serving as a director of a regulated company
